blocks.x: Student-success early warning on a governed spine, retention up 2.7 points and interventions reaching students weeks earlier

A higher-education group: Education institutions feel technology failures at enrolment and results time, when volume spikes and patience does not. The Achala program started with the peak load —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.

The baseline term measured the lateness: at-risk flags raised at week nine when withdrawal decisions were already made, advisor caseloads built on who complained loudest, and three data systems whose definitions of enrollment disagreed.
Early-warning signals existed, LMS activity, assessment grades, advising notes, but lived in systems that never spoke. The advising model was crisis response by design.

We built the student spine: LMS, SIS and advising data resolved to one student model with privacy governance signed by the faculty senate, risk signals scored weekly with the model's reasoning exposed to advisors, intervention queues ranked by reachability and need, and outcome tracking closing the loop on every intervention. Advisors act at week three, with evidence, instead of week nine, with regret.
